disposition_ledger.evidence: Design §6.2 says authorization transitions “directly to milestone commit / next skill handoff,” and FR-6.3 similarly requires moving past the review fixed point. No contract or transition limits this to taxonomy findings after active rules have passed. The pinned CLAUDE.md states that a failed constitution rule must re-enter production up to the attempt budget and only then may a human waive it, while a matched review_trigger immediately requires its own human decision. Consequently, a push-through after two review rounds could bypass repository policy rather than merely stop repetitive counter-review feedback.
disposition_ledger.rationale: Push-through must dispose only ordinary review feedback and must never bypass active constitution rules or review-trigger gates.
disposition_ledger.revision_intent: Explicitly specify in Section 6.2 and Phase 4 that push-through disposes only ordinary review findings, requiring independent resolution or explicit human waiver for constitution rules and review-trigger gates.
disposition_ledger.suggested_resolution: Specify and test that push-through disposes only ordinary review findings. Require all active constitution verdicts and review-trigger gates to be resolved independently, or model an explicit per-rule waiver after exhaustion before commit or handoff can occur.
disposition_ledger.summary: Review push-through is specified as a direct advance without preserving constitution-rule failures or triggered human constitution gates.

disposition_ledger.evidence: Design §5 routes `Triage --> EditorialProduce` but defines no outgoing transition from EditorialProduce. Phase 3’s fixed-point deliverables describe accepted, rejected/deferred, and escalated-human handling but omit accepted-editorial handling. The pinned CLAUDE.md requires a wording/formatting revision that reuses review for one hop to still receive approval of the final bytes. Implementing the documented diagram can therefore strand the workflow or incorrectly treat pre-revision review evidence as authority for revised bytes.
disposition_ledger.rationale: The editorial produce path must have an explicit outgoing transition requiring final human gate approval of revised bytes.
disposition_ledger.revision_intent: Complete the state diagram and lifecycle description in Section 5 and Phase 3 to show that EditorialProduce transitions to human gate approval of final bytes before advancing.
disposition_ledger.suggested_resolution: Define the complete editorial lifecycle: authorize exactly one non-substantive production hop, bind and validate the new bytes, prohibit another reuse hop, then require the applicable final approval gate before advancement. Add a state-transition test covering that full path.
disposition_ledger.summary: The accepted-editorial branch is a dangling state and does not preserve approval of the final revised bytes.

disposition_ledger.evidence: Design §8 declares `MAX_FALSIFIER_STRING_LENGTH` and `MAX_REASON_STRING_LENGTH` as 4096 bytes and names Zod validation as the direct assertion seam. Zod string `.max(4096)` measures JavaScript string length, not UTF-8 bytes; for example, 4096 non-ASCII characters can occupy substantially more than 4096 bytes while passing that constraint. Thus the quantitative commitment and its planned verification cannot jointly hold.
disposition_ledger.rationale: Zod .max(4096) constrains character/code-unit length, not UTF-8 byte length.
disposition_ledger.revision_intent: Update Section 8 constants table to specify character limits (Unicode code units) corresponding to Zod .max(4096) string assertions.
disposition_ledger.suggested_resolution: Either redefine both constants explicitly in Unicode code units/characters, or enforce `Buffer.byteLength(value, "utf8") <= 4096` in refinement and add boundary tests using multibyte input.
disposition_ledger.summary: The 4096-byte string limits cannot be enforced by the stated ordinary Zod string-length validation.

disposition_ledger.evidence: PRD NFR-4 requires triage evaluation and gate presentation overhead under 100ms. Design §7 maps this only to “in-memory evaluation and atomic transactional writes”; §8 omits the 100ms budget from the constants table, and none of the five phases schedules a benchmark or latency assertion. Atomic durable writes are environment-dependent, so the implementation and acceptance work can complete while the stated requirement remains unmeasured.
disposition_ledger.rationale: NFR-4 sub-100ms overhead requirement requires an auditable constants entry and scheduled measurement benchmark.
disposition_ledger.revision_intent: Add the sub-100ms budget to Section 8 constants table and schedule benchmark timing assertions in Phase 5 deliverables.
disposition_ledger.suggested_resolution: Define the measured operation boundaries, workload/state size, environment and repetition policy; add the 100ms commitment to the constants table; and schedule a benchmark or integration timing check before the phase claiming NFR-4 completion.
disposition_ledger.summary: The required sub-100ms overhead is asserted without a scheduled measurement seam.

disposition_ledger.evidence: Design §3.1 defines the new `RawReview` with `schema_version: "1"`, although it removes legacy `severity`, `blocking`, and `blocking_count`, changes verdict values, and adds required partition counts. FR-1.4 and NFR-2 require archived evidence to deserialize without data loss through discriminated compatibility schemas, but §7 merely states “discriminated unions & legacy schemas” and no discriminator separates the two version-1 shapes. Structural guessing would make future parsing, schema generation, and canonical contract selection depend on incidental fields rather than an immutable format version.
disposition_ledger.rationale: Breaking review contract changes require an explicit schema/taxonomy version discriminator to separate legacy and new review records.
disposition_ledger.revision_intent: Define an explicit version discriminator (taxonomy_version / schema_version: 2) for the 3-field review schema with distinct legacy and new discriminated union arms.
disposition_ledger.suggested_resolution: Assign the new review manifest a new schema version and define an explicit version-discriminated union with a legacy-v1 reader and new-version writer. Add archived fixtures proving exact legacy reads and rejection of mixed legacy/new shapes.
disposition_ledger.summary: The proposed incompatible review contract reuses schema version 1, leaving archived and new evidence without an explicit version discriminator.

disposition_ledger.evidence: PRD FR-7.2 requires every validation skip to expose timestamp, human reason, displaced requirements, and gate identity. Design §6.1 records only an immutable `WaiverRef` with operation and phase boundary, while Phase 4 generically mentions waiver tracking and status projection without defining displaced validation commands or requirement identifiers in the gate request, decision, or durable record. A phase-level waiver could therefore appear authorized without revealing which checks were skipped.
disposition_ledger.rationale: Validation waiver audit trail must record displaced validation requirements/commands alongside reason and gate identity.
disposition_ledger.revision_intent: Specify a canonical displaced-validation field in the validation override gate context and durable audit record in Section 6.1 and Phase 4.
disposition_ledger.suggested_resolution: Add a canonical, non-empty displaced-validation set to the override request and durable waiver record, bind it into the signed decision digest, and directly test that status reconstructs timestamp, reason, gate identity, and the exact displaced checks.
disposition_ledger.summary: The validation-waiver record does not model which required validations were displaced, so the mandated audit trail cannot be produced reliably.

disposition_ledger.evidence: Design §11 Phase 1 scopes deliverables to `src/contracts/review.ts`, `src/dispatch/cli.ts`, and schema generation, with verification "Contract tests ..., schema generator check (`npm run check:schemas`), and typecheck (`npm run typecheck`)". In the checkout at a6ebaa4e, `finding.blocking` and `finding.severity` are read outside that set: `src/review/fixed-point.ts:469` (`expected.set(..., finding.blocking)`) and `:477` (`blocking && actual.get(key) !== "rejected"`); `src/contracts/triage.ts:147` (`if (finding.blocking) blocking.add(key)`) and `:155` (accepted-editorial refusal); `src/state/request-composition.ts:498` (`if (finding.blocking) blocking.add(key)`); `src/review/counter-review.ts:792` (`allFindings.filter((f) => f.blocking).length`) and `:826`; `src/state/evidence-results.ts:285-286`; `src/review/pinned-context.ts:600-601`; `src/state/status.ts:1942-1943`; `src/contracts/renderers.ts:32`. Design §11 assigns `src/contracts/triage.ts` and `src/review/fixed-point.ts` to Phase 3 and the status/semantic files to Phase 4; `src/state/request-composition.ts`, `src/review/pinned-context.ts`, `src/contracts/renderers.ts`, and `src/state/evidence-results.ts` are assigned to no phase at all.
disposition_ledger.rationale: Phase 1 completion requires all compile-time consumers of ReviewFinding to be updated or legacy fields retained in a transitional state so typecheck passes.
disposition_ledger.revision_intent: Update Phase 1 scope to include all compile-time consumers of ReviewFinding (fixed-point, triage, request-composition, counter-review, evidence-results, pinned-context, renderers, status) so npm run typecheck succeeds at Phase 1 completion.
disposition_ledger.suggested_resolution: Either widen Phase 1 to include the compile-time consumers of `severity`/`blocking` (fixed-point, triage, request-composition, counter-review, evidence-results, pinned-context, renderers, status) so the phase ends at a typechecking repository, or state explicitly that Phase 1 adds the three new fields alongside the legacy ones and that removal happens in a named later phase, and move the `npm run typecheck` completion claim to that phase.
disposition_ledger.summary: Phase 1 removes `severity`/`blocking` from `ReviewFinding` but its scope excludes every runtime consumer of those fields, so its stated completion gate (`npm run typecheck` passing) cannot be reached inside the phase.

disposition_ledger.evidence: `src/contracts/semantic-workflow.ts:566-576` defines a second, independent finding schema (`severity: z.enum(REVIEW_FINDING_SEVERITIES)`, `blocking: z.boolean()`, plus the `only blocker findings are blocking` refinement); `:562-565` defines `triageDispositionV1Schema` with exactly three dispositions (`accepted`, `accepted-editorial`, `rejected`), which is the payload shape a producer submits; `:583` defines `publicReviewRoundV1Schema` with fixed `{ attempt, findings, blocking, accepted }` counts, consumed by `src/state/semantic-status.ts:274` (`if (blocking) round.blocking += 1`) and `:283,:297`. `src/contracts/mcp-tools.ts:150` declares `CounterReviewSuccess.verdict: "pass" | "advisory" | "fail"` with `blocking_count`, and `:360-361` enforces it in the tool output schema. Design §7 maps FR-1.5 only to `src/contracts/review.ts`, FR-3.2 only to `src/contracts/triage.ts`, and FR-7.1 to `src/state/semantic-view.ts` and `src/local/automation-status.ts`; neither `semantic-workflow.ts` nor `mcp-tools.ts` is named anywhere in §7 or §11. Consequence: the renamed verdict `review-raised` never reaches the tool result the orchestrating skill reads (it would still be validated against `"fail"`), the two new dispositions cannot be submitted through `archflow_apply`, and FR-7.1's claim_type x confidence denial metrics cannot be produced from a round contract that only counts `blocking`.
disposition_ledger.rationale: Public MCP contracts in semantic-workflow.ts and mcp-tools.ts must be mapped and updated for the 3-field taxonomy, new dispositions, and round partition counts.
disposition_ledger.revision_intent: Add src/contracts/semantic-workflow.ts and src/contracts/mcp-tools.ts to Section 7 traceability matrix and deliverables in Phase 1, Phase 3, and Phase 4.
disposition_ledger.suggested_resolution: Add `src/contracts/semantic-workflow.ts` (public finding schema, triage disposition schema, review round counts) and `src/contracts/mcp-tools.ts` (`CounterReviewSuccess.verdict`/`blocking_count`) to the traceability matrix and to the deliverables of the phases that own FR-1.5, FR-3.2, and FR-7.1, and state how the round-count shape changes to carry per-(claim_type, confidence) counts.
disposition_ledger.summary: The MCP public contract surface that skills actually read — `publicFindingV1Schema`, `triageDispositionV1Schema`, `publicReviewRoundV1Schema`, and `CounterReviewSuccess` — carries the legacy taxonomy but appears in no traceability row or phase deliverable, so FR-1.5, FR-3.2, and FR-7.1 are not reachable as mapped.

disposition_ledger.evidence: Design §3.1 defines `REVIEW_VERDICTS = ["pass", "advisory", "review-raised"]` and a `RawReview` with required `total_findings`/`partition_counts` and findings carrying no `severity`/`blocking`; §7 NFR-2 maps compatibility to "Discriminated unions & legacy schemas in `src/contracts/`". In the checkout, `src/contracts/review.ts:349` builds `reviewEvidenceSchema` as `z.discriminatedUnion("assurance", [serverAttestedReviewSchema, degradedReviewSchema])` — the discriminator is `assurance` (`server-attested` / `degraded`), which is identical for legacy and new records, so it cannot select a legacy arm; both arms are `.strict()` (`:335`, `:348`), so an archived record's `severity`, `blocking`, and `blocking_count` are rejected as unknown keys while its missing `partition_counts` is rejected as absent. Worse, `parseReviewEvidence:351-358` calls `validateReviewClaims` on every read, which recomputes the verdict via `expectedReviewSummary:146-149`; under the §3.2 replacement an archived record whose stored verdict is `"fail"` fails validation and cannot be read at all. Archived server-attested evidence is reachable from durable task state (`src/state/evidence-results.ts:285`) and from committed fixtures (`src/contracts/review.ts:253-259` notes the durable gate fixtures under `test/fixtures/contracts`). Consequence: a task holding a pre-change review can no longer load its own evidence — the same stranding failure CLAUDE.md records for the `source_evidence_set_digest` rename.
disposition_ledger.rationale: Discriminated review schema must preserve legacy review parsing and legacy verdict calculation for stored pre-change evidence.
disposition_ledger.revision_intent: Specify distinct legacy and new review schemas in Section 3 and Phase 1, with per-arm verdict validation ensuring parseReviewEvidence never breaks on legacy evidence.
disposition_ledger.suggested_resolution: Name the actual compatibility mechanism: add an explicit version discriminator (e.g. a `taxonomy_version` or a second `schema_version` value) to the review record, define a distinct legacy arm that keeps `severity`/`blocking`/`blocking_count`/`verdict: "fail"`, and specify that verdict derivation is selected per arm so `validateReviewClaims` never applies the new derivation to a legacy record. Assign this to Phase 1 and give §9 a direct test that reads a stored pre-change server-attested review.
disposition_ledger.summary: NFR-2 promises archived reviews keep parsing, but the mechanism the design names ("discriminated unions & legacy schemas") cannot discriminate legacy from new review evidence, and the single verdict-derivation function in §3.2 rejects every archived review it reads.

disposition_ledger.evidence: `src/contracts/gates.ts:27-28` defines `WaivableOperation = "review-trigger" | "adjudication-failure"` and `WaiverScope = { operation: WaivableOperation; boundary: "subject" | "phase" | "task" }`, enforced at `:245` (`operation: z.enum(["review-trigger", "adjudication-failure"])`); `"validation-override"` is not a member. `src/contracts/durable-state.ts:302-311` requires every `WaiverRef` to carry `rule_id: SafeId` and `rule_version >= 1`, and `waiverRefV1Schema:475-478` enforces both as required; §6.1 specifies neither, and a validation override answers no constitution rule. The `waiver-requested` decision payload also requires a `rule` on every gate that accepts it (`src/contracts/gates.ts:490-496`), and `:321-323`/`:364-367` refuse an eligible waiver that does not name a policy finding on the selected axis. Finally `src/review/fixed-point.ts:747-761` (`waiverInForce`) matches purely on `granted && expires && rule_id && rule_version && subject_digest && scope.operation && scope.boundary`, and `:372-376` feeds it from `state.waivers` — so a validation-override entry given a synthetic rule id that collides with a real constitution rule would silently satisfy a `constitution-review` gate, violating §9's "No Auto-Waiver by Agent" property and NFR-1.
disposition_ledger.rationale: Validation overrides are non-rule waivers and must not use rule-scoped WaiverRef in state.waivers, which could collide with constitution gate matching.
disposition_ledger.revision_intent: Specify a dedicated validation_overrides collection in TaskStateV1 (or a non-rule discriminated waiver variant) that is strictly decoupled from constitution-review gate resolution in Section 6.1 and Phase 4.
disposition_ledger.suggested_resolution: Specify the durable representation concretely: either extend `WaivableOperation` and make `rule_id`/`rule_version` optional on a new non-rule waiver variant with a discriminator that `waiverInForce` excludes from rule matching, or record validation overrides in a separate durable collection rather than `state.waivers`. Either way state the matcher change that keeps a validation override from satisfying a constitution-review waiver path, and add that non-collision property to §9 with its own test.
disposition_ledger.summary: §6.1 specifies recording the validation override as a `WaiverRef` in `state.waivers` with `scope.operation: "validation-override"`, but the durable waiver record is rule-scoped and its matcher treats any granted waiver on a (rule, subject, scope) tuple as satisfying a constitution gate, so the record as specified is both unrepresentable and unsafe.

disposition_ledger.evidence: `src/contracts/triage.ts:155` currently throws `accepted-editorial is refused for blocking finding ${key}; a blocking finding's fix is never purely editorial`, driven by `:147` (`if (finding.blocking) blocking.add(key)`); `src/state/request-composition.ts:498` mirrors the same computation. Design §3.3 and Phase 3 describe `accepted-editorial` only as "Wording/formatting fix with no behavioral or contract change -> 1-hop produce without full re-review" with no server-side refusal rule, and §9's safety matrix has no row for it. `src/review/fixed-point.ts:532-542` (`editorialRevisionPending`) then authorizes a re-entry that keeps the prior review evidence current. Consequence: after the taxonomy change the only barrier to reusing a stale review for a substantive fix is the agent's own assertion, which weakens the CLAUDE.md trust boundary that a significant revision starts a fresh review cycle while only a wording revision may reuse the prior review for one hop.
disposition_ledger.rationale: validateTriage must enforce a server-side invariant refusing accepted-editorial for defect findings to protect the trust boundary.
disposition_ledger.revision_intent: Specify in Section 3.3 and Phase 3 that validateTriage refuses accepted-editorial for any finding where claim_type is defect (or non-preference substantive finding).
disposition_ledger.suggested_resolution: State the replacement invariant explicitly in §3.3 and Phase 3 — for example, `validateTriage` refuses `accepted-editorial` for any finding whose `claim_type` is `defect` (and optionally `risk`/`gap` above a confidence threshold) — and add a direct test row for it in §9 alongside the existing triage coverage row.
disposition_ledger.summary: Removing `blocking` deletes the machine-enforced refusal of `accepted-editorial` for a blocking finding, and the design names no replacement invariant, so a `defect`/`certain` finding could take the one-hop produce path that reuses existing review evidence.

disposition_ledger.evidence: Prior triage required Section 8 to define the limits as Unicode code units corresponding to Zod `.max(4096)`. Revision 2 instead labels both `MAX_FALSIFIER_CHAR_LENGTH` and `MAX_REASON_CHAR_LENGTH` as “4096 chars” and describes their bound as “Unicode characters.” In JavaScript/Zod, an astral Unicode character such as an emoji occupies two UTF-16 code units, so a string containing 4096 such characters is 4096 Unicode code points but fails `.max(4096)`. The quantitative commitment and its direct assertion seam therefore still permit materially different implementations and boundary-test expectations.
disposition_ledger.rationale: Limits must explicitly state UTF-16 code units matching JavaScript/Zod .max(4096) string length.
disposition_ledger.revision_intent: Update Section 8 constants table to specify 4096 UTF-16 code units for MAX_FALSIFIER_STRING_LENGTH and MAX_REASON_STRING_LENGTH.
disposition_ledger.suggested_resolution: State explicitly that both limits are 4096 UTF-16 code units, or replace the Zod seam with a Unicode-code-point counter and add an astral-character boundary test matching the chosen unit.
disposition_ledger.summary: The accepted limit-unit correction was not completed: the design promises Unicode-character limits, while Zod `.max(4096)` measures UTF-16 code units.

disposition_ledger.evidence: Design §11 Phase 1 now enumerates the compile-time consumers it migrates (`src/review/fixed-point.ts`, `src/contracts/triage.ts`, `src/state/request-composition.ts`, `src/review/counter-review.ts`, `src/state/evidence-results.ts`, `src/review/pinned-context.ts`, `src/contracts/renderers.ts`, `src/state/status.ts`) and adds `src/contracts/semantic-workflow.ts` / `src/contracts/mcp-tools.ts`, with §3.3 changing `publicFindingV1Schema` (legacy fields removed) and `publicReviewRoundV1Schema` from `{ attempt, findings, blocking, accepted }` to `{ attempt, total_findings, partition_counts, accepted_count, deferred_count, escalated_human_count }`. `src/state/semantic-status.ts` is named only in §11 Phase 4 and in §7 FR-7.1, yet at commit a6ebaa4e it consumes exactly those shapes: `:266` `function reviewRounds(...): readonly PublicReviewRoundV1[]`, `:270-274` builds `{ findings, blocking, accepted }` counters, `:283` `bump(entry.attempt, entry.blocking === true, ...)`, `:297` `bump(currentAttempt, finding.blocking, ...)` (reading `blocking` off a review finding), `:320`/`:597` `publicFindingV1Schema.parse(...)`, and `:614` `publicReviewRoundV1Schema.parse(...)` cast to `PublicReviewRoundV1`. Consequence: after Phase 1 removes `blocking` from the finding type and re-shapes the round record, `finding.blocking` is a property that does not exist and the round objects no longer satisfy `PublicReviewRoundV1`, so `npm run typecheck` fails at Phase 1 completion — the same invalid-completion-state defect the previous round accepted, now relocated to the file the remediation did not move.
disposition_ledger.rationale: src/state/semantic-status.ts is a compile-time consumer of publicFindingV1Schema and publicReviewRoundV1Schema and must be migrated in Phase 1 for typecheck to pass.
disposition_ledger.revision_intent: Add src/state/semantic-status.ts to Phase 1 deliverables (adapting reviewRounds and finding projections to V2 taxonomy) while leaving new override projections in Phase 4.
disposition_ledger.suggested_resolution: Add `src/state/semantic-status.ts` to the Phase 1 deliverable list of compile-time consumers (stating that `reviewRounds` is re-shaped to emit partitioned counts and that finding projection drops `blocking`), leaving only the new override/push-through projections to Phase 4; or, alternatively, state explicitly that Phase 1 keeps the legacy public fields alongside the new ones and move the `npm run typecheck` completion claim to the phase that removes them.
disposition_ledger.summary: The remediation moved the public MCP contract surface (`publicFindingV1Schema`, `publicReviewRoundV1Schema`) into Phase 1, but `src/state/semantic-status.ts` — the only producer of those shapes — is still assigned to Phase 4, so Phase 1's stated completion gate (`npm run typecheck` passing) again cannot be reached inside the phase.
